explanation: Its red cells carry none of the A, B or RhD markers that can trigger a dangerous reaction. AB positive is the opposite: people with it can receive red cells of any type.

claims.text: O negative is known as the universal donor type, because its red cells can be given to almost any recipient.
Red cells of types AB positive, A negative and B positive cannot safely be given to every recipient.
O negative red cells lack the A, B and RhD antigens.
People with AB positive blood can receive red cells of any ABO and RhD type.

evidence.restatement: Group O RhD-negative red cells can be given to almost any recipient, so O negative is called the universal donor.
AB positive, A negative and B positive red cells carry A, B or RhD antigens that some recipients would attack.
O negative red cells carry neither A nor B antigens and no RhD antigen.
AB positive recipients have no anti-A, anti-B or anti-D antibodies, so they can receive red cells of any ABO and RhD type.
O negative red cells are the universal donor type for red-cell transfusion.
AB positive, A negative and B positive red cells are incompatible with some recipients.
